message: A _ref to a .njk file renders at build. A .yaml.njk, .yml.njk or .json.njk file is parsed into config afterwards, so operators written in it are ordinary runtime operators; any other .njk file renders to text, where an operator would never run - the build rejects that with the ref-njk-runtime-operator check. Use the _nunjucks operator over a .txt file for a template that needs runtime values.
A _ref to a .js file imports it as a module rather than reading it as text. Name the file .js.txt to read its source.

This request runs over a tenant-walled connection. The wall injects { $match: { <tenant field> } } into the top-level pipeline and into every $lookup / $unionWith sub-pipeline, so a lookup only ever sees documents that carry the tenant field. The build now rejects a lookup into a collection declared shared, so run that lookup over the shared connection and pass tenant facts in the payload instead.
:reject is the routine's reply, not an exception. A :catch never runs for it, :finally does, and :throw is the caught path.
